items: Java compiles to **bytecode**, which the **JVM** executes: that indirection is what makes Java portable.
Use the **JDK** to write Java; the **JRE** only runs it.
Every program lives in a **class**, and execution begins at **`main`**.
The file name must match the public class name, and every statement ends with a semicolon.
**Identifiers** are case sensitive, cannot start with a digit, and cannot be reserved words.
**Syntax errors** stop the build; **logical errors** let the program run and give wrong answers.
**Comments** are ignored by the compiler: write them to explain *why*.
